ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Martin Luther — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Six-week review: attacks, MRI result, thiazide and sertraline safety, mood, and the passed stone

text.paragraph: Six-week review of Ménière disease, depression and the passed stone. [S]

Professor Luther returns six weeks after the consultation. He has had one attack since then, of about two hours, ten days before his preventive visit, and none in the three weeks since. He keeps sodium down at home and has cut coffee to a cup a day. Between attacks he feels slightly unsteady when he turns quickly or walks in the dark. The MRI was done last week. The stone he passed nine days after his sick visit has been analyzed. He has taken hydrochlorothiazide and sertraline 50 mg daily; the loose stools on starting sertraline have settled. He has attended five therapy sessions and has begun to plan small pleasant activities each day. His sleep is better, and he has no thoughts of harming himself. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1527-09-22; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: No nystagmus; head impulse test normal; tandem gait slightly unsteady; Romberg steady on a firm surface, sways on foam with eyes closed
Brighter, reactive affect; no suicidal ideation

Recurrent attacks of spinning vertigo for about three months, the worst twelve days ago, lasting hours, with roaring tinnitus, fullness and muffled hearing in the left ear and nausea, the tinnitus persisting between attacks; with low mood, poor sleep and loss of interest; cause not established at intake: an inner-ear disorder suspected, with vestibular migraine, vestibular schwannoma and posterior circulation stroke to be excluded and depression to be assessed; otology consultation requested
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to his documented attacks of April and July 1527; superseded by the diagnoses at the second visit.

Ménière disease of the left ear, definite (AAO-HNS 1521 and Bárány Society criteria), with low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss and persistent tinnitus in the left ear; vestibular migraine considered and judged unlikely as the main cause; vestibular schwannoma excluded by MRI
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the otology consultation, linked to his documented attacks and to the retrospective diagnosis of Ménière disease (R).

Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate (DSM-5-TR), with low mood, poor sleep, loss of interest, guilt and fatigue for about two months, after earlier periods of spiritual crisis and low mood; no suicidal ideation
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis linked to his documented Anfechtungen and low periods; not a claim that he was so diagnosed; the retrospective psychiatric readings are disputed (R).
Urinary stone disease: one stone passed spontaneously last year after severe pain; stone type and metabolic risk not yet known at intake
S — Synthetic modern problem anchored to his documented first stone in 1526.

Right distal ureteral stone, 5 mm, at the ureterovesical junction, with mild right hydronephrosis and renal colic; no infection; kidney function normal; managed with naproxen and tamsulosin; passed nine days later; resolved
S — Synthetic acute problem anchored to his documented recurrent stones; this episode is not a historical claim.

list.item:
Ménière disease of the left ear, improving (H81.02). One shorter attack in six weeks on the salt limit and thiazide. The MRI shows no vestibular schwannoma or other lesion. Sodium 136, potassium 3.7 mmol/L and calcium 10.0 mg/dL on the thiazide with sertraline; uric acid 7.4 mg/dL, up from 6.9, as expected with a thiazide, without gout. The mild unsteadiness between attacks fits incomplete compensation in the left inner ear. [S]
Continue hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg and the salt limit.
Vestibular rehabilitation with a home program from a vestibular physical therapist.
Repeat audiogram at the next visit.

Urinary stone disease (Z87.442). The stone analysis shows calcium oxalate monohydrate (80 percent) with calcium phosphate (20 percent). Ultrasound shows no hydronephrosis and no remaining stones. With two stones he is a recurrent calcium stone former, so a 24-hour urine is indicated to guide prevention. [S]
24-hour urine for volume, calcium, oxalate, citrate, sodium, uric acid and creatinine, on his usual diet, before the next visit.
Keep drinking enough to pass at least 2.5 liters of urine a day.

Recurrent depression, improving (F33.1). PHQ-9 10, from 15 at intake, after five weeks of sertraline 50 mg and five therapy sessions; not yet a 50 percent response. Sodium normal on the SSRI with the thiazide. [S]
Continue sertraline 50 mg and weekly therapy; consider 100 mg if the PHQ-9 is not clearly lower at the next visit.
Safety plan reviewed and unchanged; 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and the clinic number confirmed.
